parsed.use_case: A search or messaging service can check whether a tokenized query or incoming text can be fully explained by entries in its approved vocabulary, with entries reusable across the text. This is useful for validating dictionary-backed commands or detecting whether a string consists entirely of known terms.
system_examples: Spell-checking and text-input systems — determine whether a string can be split into valid dictionary words, including compounds.
Command parsers and protocol validators — verify that an input is composed entirely of recognized, reusable tokens.
parsed.explanation: Dynamic programming over string positions checks whether each prefix can be formed from a previously reachable position plus a dictionary word, typically in O(n·L) time with efficient word lookup, where n is the string length and L bounds candidate word lengths. This avoids enumerating exponentially many possible segmentations; the core problem is also a useful teaching model for tokenization, though production parsers often add rules beyond a plain word list.
